 Plaskett taps ex-DPNR chief convicted of bribery, obstruction for chief of staff 
 By SUZANNE CARLSON
Daily News Staff 
 Suzanne Carlson 
 Author email 
 Nov 6, 2026 
 Nov 6, 2026 
 Facebook 
 Twitter 
 WhatsApp 
 SMS 
 Email 
 Facebook 
 Twitter 
 WhatsApp 
 SMS 
 Email 
 Print 
 Copy article link 
 Save 
 Governor-elect Stacey Plaskett has chosen Dean Plaskett to serve as chief of staff for her transition team, despite his criminal history of public corruption while serving as commissioner of the Department of Planning and Natural Resources.
 Federal prosecutors indicted 61-year-old Plaskett in 2007 alongside Marc Biggs, former Property and Procurement Commissioner, and both were convicted in 2008 after a two-week trial.
 Plaskett issued a statement Thursday that briefly addressed Dean Plaskett’s criminal history.
 “Dean Plaskett’s past conviction is a matter of public record. He has served his sentence, and that chapter of his life does not erase the experience, knowledge, and abilities he brings to his work,” according to the press release.
 “We believe individuals should be judged not only by their past, but also by their capacity to contribute meaningfully today. As Chief of Staff, Mr. Plaskett will be held to the same standards of professionalism, integrity, and accountability expected of everyone entrusted with serving the people of the Virgin Islands,” she added.
 Jurors found them guilty “of demanding and accepting bribes and kickbacks in connection with the award of a $650,000 government contract to a shell company. Plaskett was also convicted on two counts of obstruction of justice, stemming from his efforts to conceal the bribery and kickback scheme from federal and local investigators as well as a grand jury,” according to the U.S. Department of Justice. “Specifically, evidence at trial revealed that Plaskett attempted to have fictitious documents created and backdated to falsely document work never done by the same shell company on a different government contract valued at $130,000.”
 Several other government officials pleaded guilty to their role in the bribery and kickback scheme, which began in 2000 and was first revealed in a 2005 Daily News special investigative report, “Contracts and Cronies.”
 The 3rd Circuit affirmed Plaskett’s convictions in 2010, writing that he and Biggs “were charged with participating in an elaborate bribery and kickback scheme with other government officials and complicit business owners. The indictment alleged that the members of the scheme used fictitious and real companies to obtain government contracts worth more than $1.4 million and progress payments of more than $1 million, despite little or no contract performance.”
 Plaskett was sentenced to nine years in federal prison and ordered to pay a money judgment of $1.09 million. That figure had grown to $1.6 million as of 2011 and was continuing to accrue interest, according to a filing by prosecutors.
 Governor-elect Plaskett’s transition team did not respond to questions from The Daily News, including an inquiry about whether Dean Plaskett has satisfied the money judgment.
 She also did not respond to questions about reports that they are cousins.
 Dean Plaskett served as DPNR commissioner from 1999 through 2006, and was also chairman of the V.I. Economic Development Authority governing board from 2001 through 2006, according to his LinkedIn profile.
 The press release issued by the transition team noted that “Plaskett holds a juris doctorate (JD) degree and brings experience in public administration and government operations.” The statement did not mention that he was disbarred by the V.I. Supreme Court in 2012 because of the nature of his criminal convictions and the ethical violations they represented.
 Plaskett was released from federal custody in June 2016, and his defense attorney, Gordon Rhea, said he wanted to “remain private” and declined interview requests. Rhea currently serves as V.I. attorney general.
 Plaskett returned to the territory after his release from prison and started a company, The Plaskett Consultancy, which is still listed as his current occupation on LinkedIn, and specializes in “Economic Development Authority compliance; Coastal Zone Management permitting; building permitting; Environmental Protection issues; and legislative and executive branch administration.”
 Department of Licensing and Consumer Affairs Commissioner Devin Carrington told The Daily News at the time that he made the decision to grant Plaskett a business license because “we felt the consumer would not be at risk,” and “it was important to me to give the gentleman an opportunity to earn a living.”
 The Property and Procurement commissioner at the time, Randolph Bennett, said The Plaskett Consultancy was welcome to do business with the private sector, but would not be awarded any government contracts, “not under my watch.”
 According to the transition team press release, which was distributed by Tionee Scotland, Erwin Raphael has been named Transition Director.
 Scotland’s husband, Ashley Scotland, will serve as Deputy Transition Director alongside Cosme Christian, who is currently serving as Lt. Gov.-elect Milton Potter’s chief of staff as he finishes his term as Senate president.
 The transition leadership team also includes:
 • Kurell Sheridan, Chief of Operations
 • Chivonne Thomas, Legal Director
 • Lorna A.C. Thomas, Communications Director
 • Shani DeWindt, Communications Co-Director
 • Renee McAlpin Petersen, Community Outreach Coordinator
 • Elizabeth Centeno, Landing Team Coordinator
 In addition, the governor-elect and lieutenant governor-elect announced the leadership of the inaugural planning effort:
 • Jonathan Buckney-Small and Paulette Potter, Honorary Inaugural Chairs
 • Jerry Garcia, Inaugural Chair
 • Nellie Varlack, Inaugural Director, St. Thomas
 • Shamari Haynes, Inaugural Director, St. Croix
 • Leona Smith, Inaugural Director, St. John
 “The transition process will include a comprehensive review of government operations, the development of priorities for the incoming administration, and the identification of qualified individuals interested in public service. Fourteen policy committees will examine critical areas, including energy, healthcare, education, housing, public safety, infrastructure, and economic development,” according to the press release.
 Residents can learn more about the transition leadership, submit their qualifications for consideration, and follow announcements at www.plaskettpottertransition.com .
